title: Purity of the top affine-curve factor
statement:
Let $C_0$ be a smooth affine curve over $k_0=\mathbf F_q$ (an affine
$k_0$-scheme, smooth of relative dimension one) and let $\mathcal E$ be
a lisse Weil sheaf on $C_0$, punctually $\iota$-pure of weight zero.
Then $H_c^2(C,\mathcal E)$ is $\iota$-pure of weight two over $k_0$:
every Frobenius eigenvalue on it has $\iota$-modulus $q$.

proof.text: If $C_0$ is geometrically connected, apply [lem-a1-affine-hc2-pure] with $w=0$. Its hypotheses are precisely smoothness, affineness, geometric connectedness, lissity and punctual purity of weight zero. It gives purity of $H_c^2$ of weight $0+2=2$; [def-weil-frobenius-module-weights] says exactly that every Frobenius eigenvalue has $\iota$-modulus $q$.

Apply [lem-zl-affine-geometric-components-finite-extension] to $C_0$. Choose $e\geq1$ and write $C_{0,e}=C_0\times_{k_0}\mathbf F_{q^e}=\coprod_{i\in I}C_{i,e}$. Each $C_{i,e}$ is nonempty, smooth of relative dimension one, affine and geometrically connected over $\mathbf F_{q^e}$. Put $C_i=C_{i,e}\times_{\mathbf F_{q^e}}k$. Thus $C=\coprod_iC_i$, and $q^e$-Frobenius preserves every $C_i$.

source.place: Second paragraph, first four sentences: descent of the geometric components

proof.text: Use [lem-zl-weil-constant-extension-frobenius] with $X_0=C_0$ and $\mathcal F=\mathcal E$. The resulting $\mathcal E^{(e)}$ is lisse and punctually pure of weight zero over $\mathbf F_{q^e}$, and its cohomological Frobenius is $F^e$ on the original coefficient space. Restrict it to $C_{i,e}$, obtaining $\mathcal E_i$. Lissity is local, as in [def-pod-lisse-l-adic-sheaves]. Each closed point of the open and closed subscheme $C_{i,e}$ is the same closed point of $C_{0,e}$ with the same residue field and stalk operator, so [def-weil-punctual-weights] gives punctual purity of $\mathcal E_i$ with the unchanged weight zero.

source.place: Second paragraph: preservation of punctual weight zero under the extension and restriction

proof.text: For each $i$, apply [lem-a1-affine-hc2-pure] over the finite base field $\mathbf F_{q^e}$, with $w=0$ and with the smooth geometrically connected affine curve $C_{i,e}$ and sheaf $\mathcal E_i$ from steps 2 and 3. It gives purity of $H_c^2(C_i,\mathcal E_i)$ of weight two. Thus every eigenvalue of its $q^e$-Frobenius has modulus $(q^e)^{2/2}=q^e$ by [def-weil-frobenius-module-weights].

source.place: Second paragraph: apply the connected argument to each component

proof.text:
Here is the direct-sum identification used in the blueprint. Write $a:C\to s=\operatorname{Spec}k$, $j_i:C_i\hookrightarrow C$, and $a_i=aj_i$. The coefficient-category equivalence in [lem-pur-finite-clopen-derived-decomposition] and the exceptional restriction comparisons in [lem-pur-finite-clopen-exceptional-restriction], together with the constructible exceptional adjunction in [prop-functor-package], give, naturally in $L$,
$$\operatorname{Hom}(Ra_!\mathcal E^{(e)},L)=\operatorname{Hom}(\mathcal E^{(e)},Ra^!L)=\prod_i\operatorname{Hom}(\mathcal E_i,Ra_i^!L)=\prod_i\operatorname{Hom}(Ra_{i!}\mathcal E_i,L).$$
The final expression is the universal property of $\bigoplus_iRa_{i!}\mathcal E_i$, so these objects are canonically isomorphic. Evaluate at $s$ and take degree-two cohomology as in [def-weil-ordinary-compact-cohomology]:
$$H_c^2(C,\mathcal E^{(e)})\simeq\bigoplus_iH_c^2(C_i,\mathcal E_i).$$
All component inclusions are defined over $\mathbf F_{q^e}$. Equivariance of adjunction and composition comparisons in [lem-fix-weil-operations] makes this isomorphism $q^e$-Frobenius equivariant. The empty-family clause of the clopen equivalence gives zero cohomology for $C=\varnothing$. All exceptional adjunctions here are on the stated bounded constructible field-coefficient categories; no unrestricted ambient adjoint is used.

source.place: Second paragraph: take the direct sum of compactly supported cohomology; empty curve

proof.text: Let $v\ne0$ be an eigenvector of $F$ on $H_c^2(C,\mathcal E)$ with eigenvalue $\lambda$. Iterating $Fv=\lambda v$ gives $F^ev=\lambda^ev$. Under the Frobenius-equivariant direct sum of step 5, at least one component $v_i$ is nonzero and satisfies $F_i v_i=\lambda^ev_i$. Step 4 gives $|\iota(\lambda^e)|=q^e$. Multiplicativity yields $|\iota(\lambda)|^e=q^e$; since $e\geq1$, $q>0$ and $|\iota(\lambda)|\geq0$, strict increase of the positive integral power implies $|\iota(\lambda)|=q$. This is exactly weight two by [def-weil-frobenius-module-weights]. If the coefficient space is zero there is no nonzero eigenvector and the assertion is vacuous. This calculation needs neither diagonalizability nor any assertion that $F$ itself fixes each component.

source.place: Second paragraph, final four sentences: descent of the equality of weights

blueprint_update.statement:
Let $C_0$ be a smooth affine curve over $k_0=\mathbf F_q$ (an affine
$k_0$-scheme, smooth of relative dimension one) and let $\mathcal E$ be
a lisse Weil sheaf on $C_0$, punctually $\iota$-pure of weight zero.
Then $H_c^2(C,\mathcal E)$ is $\iota$-pure of weight two over $k_0$:
every Frobenius eigenvalue on it has $\iota$-modulus $q$.

proof.text:
First assume that $C_0$ is geometrically connected. Then
[lem-a1-affine-hc2-pure], applied with $w=0$, shows that
$H_c^2(C,\mathcal E)$ is $\iota$-pure of weight two in
[def-weil-frobenius-module-weights]: every Frobenius eigenvalue on it
has $\iota$-modulus $q$.

For a general smooth affine curve, choose a finite extension
$\mathbf F_{q^e}/\mathbf F_q$ over which all its finitely many
geometric connected components are defined. This is possible because
each open and closed component is specified by an idempotent in its
affine coordinate ring after base change to $\overline{\mathbf F}_q$,
and the finitely many coefficients of these idempotents lie in a
finite extension. Over $\mathbf F_{q^e}$ the curve is a finite
disjoint union of geometrically connected smooth affine curves.
The restricted sheaves remain punctually pure of weight zero:
if a closed point $z$ of the base change maps to $x\in C_0$,
the Frobenius on its stalk is $F_x^{[\kappa(z):\kappa(x)]}$.
Every eigenvalue is therefore a positive integral power of an
eigenvalue of $F_x$, and still has modulus one, as required by
[def-weil-punctual-weights]. Apply the preceding argument to
each component and take the direct sum of their compactly supported
cohomology. Every eigenvalue of $F^e$ on this sum has modulus
$q^e$. If $\lambda$ is an eigenvalue of $F$, then
$\lambda^e$ is an eigenvalue of $F^e$, so
$\lvert\iota(\lambda)\rvert^e=q^e$, and
$\lvert\iota(\lambda)\rvert=q$. The empty curve has zero
cohomology, so its assertion is vacuous.
